How to add a tool to a go module in Go 1.24

by Joe Blogs

In Go 1.24, a new command called go tools has been introduced. This command is designed to help users manage and run various Go tools that are not part of the standard library or the core Go toolchain.

I was using an existing program goose to manage database migrations, but it was not part of the standard Go toolchain. With the introduction of go tools, I can now easily install and run goose as a Go tool.

can install goose using the command:

go get -tool github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose

usage: go tool [-n] command [args...]
                                                                                                                                                          
Tool runs the go tool command identified by the arguments.
                                                                                                                                                          
Go ships with a number of builtin tools, and additional tools
may be defined in the go.mod of the current module.
                                                                                                                                                          
With no arguments it prints the list of known tools.
                                                                                                                                                          
The -n flag causes tool to print the command that would be
executed but not execute it.
                                                                                                                                                          
For more about each builtin tool command, see 'go doc cmd/<command>'.

References

  • https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.24#tools
  • https://blog.howardjohn.info/posts/go-tools-command/
